description: Sync the Notion pages and databases you share with HydraDB, one searchable document per page.
intro: The Notion connector reads the databases and top-level pages you share with its integration. Each page becomes one document: a database row, a selected page, and every sub-page under them.
Each sub-page is linked to the page it sits under, so a page tree stays connected.

connect.auth: Notion uses an internal integration token.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: A Notion internal integration token. It starts with `secret_` or `ntn_`.

permissions.name: Read content
permissions.text: required. Lets HydraDB search, read pages and blocks, and query databases.

permissions.name: Read user information without email
permissions.text: optional. Lets HydraDB check the token and show who created a page.

steps.title: Create an integration
steps.text: In Notion, create an internal integration with the Read content capability, and copy its token.

steps.title: Share content with it
steps.text: Share each database and page you want synced with the integration. Discovery lists only what the integration can see.

steps.title: Select resources
steps.text: Discover lists every database the integration can see, and every page that sits at the top of the workspace. Select at least one: a sync needs a selected resource.

documents.name: Pages
documents.one_document: One Notion page: a database row, a selected page, or any sub-page under them. A sub-page is its own document, not part of its parent's text.
documents.title: The page's title. A page without a title uses its Notion id.
documents.text: The page title at the top, the creator as an `Author` line, and the plain text of the page's blocks in order, one block per line: paragraphs, headings, bulleted and numbered lists, to-dos, toggles, quotes, callouts and code. Text inside toggles and callouts is included.
documents.date: When the page was last edited.
documents.files: Images and files are kept as links to the original. Text in images can be added when HydraDB's image reading is available. The text of PDF and Word files is not guaranteed to be read.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: Names the page in results, and is written at the top of its text.

attributes.name: Page text
attributes.text: The block text described above. This is what a query matches.

attributes.name: created_by
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: The creator's display name, or their Notion id if the name cannot be read. It is the `Author` line of the text, and the graph records the page as written by that person.

attributes.name: last_edited_time
attributes.text: When the page was last edited. It is the document date, and it is not part of the text.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.notion_page_id
attributes.text: The page's Notion id. Limits a query to one page.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: For a sub-page, the page it sits under. Links the two, so a page tree is connected in the graph.

attributes.name: created_by_email
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: The creator's email, when Notion returns one. It lets the graph recognise the same person across tools.

attributes.name: mentions
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: People @mentioned in the page. The graph records each as mentioned by the page.

attributes.name: last_edited_by
attributes.text: The Notion user id of the last editor. It is not turned into a name or a person.

attributes.name: Database properties
attributes.text: Property values other than the title, such as status, owner, dates and tags, are not read.

attributes.name: Comments
attributes.text: Comments on pages are not read.

connections: A sub-page to the page it sits under.
No links from Notion pages to other tools. In the other direction, GitHub issues, pull requests and comments that link to a Notion page are linked to it.
people: The page's creator, with an email when Notion returns one.
graph.from_text: Everything in the page text: topics, and people or projects named in plain text rather than @mentioned. Database properties are not read, so structure kept only in database columns is not available.

notes: Notion's page sharing is not read.

sync.first_sync: A database reaches back 30 days by last edited time by default, set by `lookback_days`. A selected page and its sub-pages are walked on every sync.
sync.changes: For a database, rows edited since the last sync are read again in full, with their sub-pages. For a selected page, the whole tree is walked on every sync and pages edited since the last sync are sent.
sync.edits: An edited page is sent again and replaces its document. A sub-page under a database row is picked up only when the row itself is edited.
sync.deletes: Pages deleted or unshared in Notion are not removed. They stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: Sub-pages are followed up to 10 levels deep, and blocks up to 20 levels deep.
A sub-page or block that Notion now refuses or cannot find is skipped instead of failing its page.

not_synced: Database property values other than the title.
Pages and databases not shared with the integration.
Text in unsupported blocks, such as table rows, equations, embeds and bookmarks.
Deletions: deleted pages stay in HydraDB.
questions: What does our onboarding page say about laptop setup?
Which Notion pages did Priya create?
What sub-pages sit under the Engineering Handbook page?

good_to_know.title: Database columns are not synced.
good_to_know.text: A database row brings in its title and page text only. Status, owner, dates and tags are not read.

good_to_know.title: Edits to a sub-page under a database row can be missed.
good_to_know.text: They are picked up when the row itself is edited. Pages you select directly do not have this problem, because they are walked on every sync.

good_to_know.title: Only the last 30 days of a database come in first.
